:::{#thm-distance-corrects-errors}
#### Minimum distance sets how many errors a code handles

Let a [block code](#def-block-code) have
[minimum distance](#def-hamming-distance) $d$,
and let $y$ be a codeword $c$ with some of its symbols changed.

1. If at most $d - 1$ symbols changed and at least one did,
   then $y$ is not a codeword, so the receiver detects the error.

2. If at most $t \eqdef \floor{(d - 1)/2}$ symbols changed,
   then $c$ is the only codeword nearest to $y$ in Hamming distance,
   so decoding $y$ to its nearest codeword corrects the errors.

:::

::: {.proof}
For part 1, $0 < \hamdist{c}{y} \le d - 1 < d$,
so $y \ne c$.
If $y$ were another codeword $c'$, then $\hamdist{c}{c'} = \hamdist{c}{y} < d$,
which the minimum distance rules out.

For part 2, Hamming distance satisfies the triangle inequality,
since a position where $c$ and $c'$ differ is a position
where $y$ differs from $c$ or from $c'$.
So for any codeword $c' \ne c$,

$$
\hamdist{c'}{y}
\ge \hamdist{c}{c'} - \hamdist{c}{y}
\ge d - t
\ge t + 1
> \hamdist{c}{y},
$$

where $d - t \ge t + 1$ because $2t \le d - 1$.

:::
